Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
619 AM CDT Wed Jul 29 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Generally hot and dry through the end of the week, with heat 
  index values close to Heat Advisory thresholds. 

- Isolated shower or thunderstorm possible along the sea breeze
  boundary today. 

- Chance of isolated to scattered showers/thunderstorms increases
  by the weekend / early next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1200 AM CDT Wed Jul 29 2026

North America is under an amplified mid/upper flow pattern as 
evident on GOES water vapor imagery and 500 MB RAP analysis. The 
pattern over Texas is dominated by a stout mid/upper ridge, centered 
over New Mexico and with a ridge axis that extends deep into central 
Canada. This ridge will be the primary driver our weather, keeping 
conditions hot and relatively dry through the end of the week. 
Global ensembles suggest the ridge will build further over region, 
w/ ensemble mean 500MB height rising from ~592dm to ~595dm between 
now and Friday. These same ensembles also indicate a slight climb in 
850 MB temps, rising from ~20-22C to ~23-25C over the next few days, 
portending to building heat at the surface. Temperates have already 
been hot, though not quite as hot as our friend the NBM has 
suggested. Our forecast the last few days has leaned more on the 
NBM, resulting in a slightly hotter forecast than reality. 
Therefore, I mixed in some 25th percentile NBM into our temperature 
grids. But don't get too excited about the "cooler" guidance. Our 
forecast high temperatures remain near 100 degrees through week's 
end. Afternoon dew points are forecast to mix down into the upper 
60s to low 70s, equating to heat indices in the 105-108 degree range 
(Heat Advisory criteria is 108). Heat indices will likely be close 
to advisory criteria through the end of the week. Some possibility 
of even lower dew points on Friday if the global deterministic 
guidance has their way. 

Despite the dry signal in the pattern, there is some hope for rain. 
Hi-res forecast soundings indicate capping aloft today. But I am 
unconvinced that the cap will too strong to prevent an isolated 
shower or thunderstorm along the sea breeze boundary. Sfc 
convergence could be particularly strong in the vicinity where the
Galveston Bay breeze converges with the ambient southwesterly 
flow. HRRR and RRFS suggest a brief thunderstorm or two will occur
in Harris County this afternoon. In addition, there may be hope 
for some isolated to scattered showers/storm by the weekend or 
early next week as the mid/upper pattern retrogrades, shifting the
downstream troughing over eastern CONUS westward. Global ensemble
means drop 500 MB heights to ~587dm, while also introducing some 
PVA into the area from the east. There is even some potential for 
a weak backdoor front to push into our neck of the woods by Sunday
and Monday. 

Self

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 619 AM CDT Wed Jul 29 2026

A forecast of persistence looks tough to beat. A few isolated 
patches of higher end MVFR cigs/fog north and west of the metro 
area will burn off early this morning, with VFR conditions 
anticipated area-wide for the rest of the day. Will keep an eye 
on the possibility of a late day seabreeze/baybreeze shower or 
tstm around the metro (similar to yesterday), but will not include
the mention in the 12z TAFs.  47 

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1140 PM CDT Tue Jul 28 2026

Light to moderate southwest winds are expected through Friday.
Winds may become more southerly during the afternoon and hours.
Seas are expected to average 2 to 4 feet. Southwest winds and seas
are expected to increase over the weekend, possible nearing Small
Craft Advisory thresholds in some areas. We also expect an
increase chance of isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms
by the weekend and early next week.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
632 AM CDT Wed Jul 29 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dangerous heat continues with temperatures in the upper 90s to 
  100s and heat indices of 105-110F.

- A Heat Advisory is in effect for Areas east of I-49 and along
  the Atchafalaya.

- Rain chances and slightly cooler temperatures arrive late in the
  work week and into the weekend. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(Tonight through next Tuesday)
Issued at 1044 PM CDT Tue Jul 28 2026

Bulk of forecast considerations tonight were taken in by heat
indices tomorrow (Wednesday.) The persistence forecast will
prevail until tomorrow with the start of a pattern change taking
place sometime Thursday. High pressure regime remains in place,
and in fact, may be enhanced some on Wednesday. Upper low pressure
and trof descend from the northeast US, which lays the framework
for later waves to erode upper high pressure. In the meantime, it
appears the trof only acts to compress high pressure over the
central US, and ultimately increase heights on Wednesday. While
this will likely result in slightly higher temps Wed, it will also
mean mixing once again. Since the airmass overtop the region mixed
out quickly before those advisory-criteria indices really set in,
it meant that most of the region stayed at and under 108 today.
Since the same scenario may play out Wed, the bulk of the area 
was left out of an advisory. Those in Alexandria and along the 
Atchafalaya may hit 108 to 110, even with mixing, so those areas 
did get an advisory for the day. 

There is the part of the seabreeze pushing in during the early
afternoon which may poke heat indices up a skosh, but if it was 
like today, even that moisture plume could be mixed down quickly. 
Unless there is a notable change in presentation or forecast 
overnight, the advisory will stand as-is. But adjustments may come
as deemed necessary. 

High pressure will try to hang on into Thursday which may bring
about this conversation again, but considering the increase in
moisture that's anticipated with the approaching east trof, there
could be enough cloud cover to tamp temps down from the needed
highs to bring about advisory criteria Thursday to the end of the
week. 

Residual high will also deflect majority of rain chances to the
east until it can back off sometime later Thursday or Friday. 

11/Calhoun

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 631 AM CDT Wed Jul 29 2026

With light winds and clear skies, to go along with a very humid
air mass, some patchy fog is occurring at terminals this morning
that will last until shortly after sunrise. Otherwise, VFR
conditions expected through the day. 

07/Rua

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1044 PM CDT Tue Jul 28 2026

Low seas and moderate onshore winds will prevail to the end of the
work week as high pressure largely remains in charge. High
pressure will begin backing into central Texas late Thursday into
Friday, igniting a pressure gradient and increasing easterly
winds. This may result in a period of Small Craft Advisory
conditions and very likely will signal the return of some rain
chances over coastal waters. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1044 PM CDT Tue Jul 28 2026

High pressure will hang on into Wednesday and likely into much of
Thursday, continuing the anomalously hot and dry pattern these
days. Daytime RH minimums will vary in the 45 to 60 percent range
through the end of the week, increasing into the weekend with the
return of rain chances.
